archon-boot/doctor.ts

deno task stolos boot doctor (spec 004): one read-only look at this boot machine, with the fix for each problem: the checkout (hosts install from GitHub, so local changes must be pushed), the model, secrets, Ubuntu's files, the network, the ports, and the firewall. It changes nothing.

Functions

f
doctor(o: { port: number; send?: string; embedded?: boolean; }): Promise<number>

Run the boot doctor: check the checkout, model, secrets, Ubuntu's files, network, ports and firewall, printing a fix for each problem. Read-only. port is the boot server's HTTP port, send mails the findings, and embedded joins a caller's run (vault restore) instead of starting one. Returns the exit code (nonzero when a check fails).

archon-boot/firewall.ts

Firewall check for boot serve (spec 004): warn, with the exact command, when this machine's firewall would block servers from reaching TFTP (UDP) or HTTP (TCP). Read-only: it never changes a firewall rule. Windows Defender Firewall, ufw, and firewalld; anything else is not checked.

archon-boot/guard.ts

Spec 051: the blank-disk guard. Before Ubuntu's installer touches a disk, it reports the machine's own facts (from its firmware tables, /proc, and its disks) to this boot server, which answers "ok" or "stop: why". The install goes on by itself only when every disk is blank, when a person confirmed with --confirm-destroy <host>, or when the machine is this host already (it installed as this host, or boot reinstall reached it over SSH). Anything else stops before a byte is written, and the boot window says what the machine holds and the one command that lets it go on.

bootMac: string | undefined,
reg?: Pick<HostRegistration, "mac" | "macSource">
): GuardDecision

Whether this install may go on (see the header).

Variables

v
GUARD_SCRIPT: `#!/bin/sh # archon-boot (spec 051): before any disk is touched, report this machine's # facts to the boot server and do what it answers. Nothing here writes a disk. B="$1" F=/tmp/archon-facts { for k in sys_vendor product_name product_serial board_vendor board_name; do echo "$k=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/$k 2>/dev/null)" done echo "mem_kib=$(awk '/^MemTotal:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)" echo "cpus=$(nproc 2>/dev/null)" # Disks (not RAM disks, loops, or optical drives, by their fixed majors; zram by # name: its major, like virtio's and NVMe's, is assigned at boot). lsblk -dnbro NAME,SIZE,TYPE,TRAN -e 1,7,11 2>/dev/null | awk '$3 == "disk" && $1 !~ /^zram/ { print "disk=" $1 " " $2 " " $4 }' # What is on them, probed on the disks themselves (wipefs): udev's database, # which lsblk reads, is not filled in yet this early. Any partition the kernel # sees counts too. A disk that cannot be probed counts as not blank. for d in $(lsblk -dnro NAME,TYPE -e 1,7,11 2>/dev/null | awk '$2 == "disk" && $1 !~ /^zram/ { print "/dev/" $1 }'); do command -v wipefs >/dev/null || { echo "signature=$d unchecked (no wipefs)"; continue; } for x in $d $(lsblk -nrpo NAME,TYPE "$d" 2>/dev/null | awk '$2 == "part" { print $1 }'); do [ "$x" = "$d" ] || echo "signature=$x partition" wipefs -n --noheadings -O DEVICE,TYPE "$x" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NF > 1 { print "signature=" $1 " " $2 }' || echo "signature=$x unchecked" done done } >"$F" A=$(curl -fsS --noproxy "*" -m 30 -X POST -H 'content-type: text/plain' --data-binary @"$F" "\${B}facts") || A="stop: the boot server did not answer, so nothing was erased (is deno task stolos boot serve running?)" case "$A" in ok*) exit 0 ;; esac echo "archon: $A" | tee /dev/console echo "archon: nothing was written to any disk; this machine powers off in 30 seconds." | tee /dev/console sleep 30 poweroff -f `

Run by the installer (early-commands) with the host's install URL. Facts only, as key=value lines; the decision is the boot server's. It fails closed: no answer, no install.

archon-boot/http.ts

A small HTTP/1.1 server for archon-boot (spec 004). Deno.serve sends header names in lowercase, which HTTP allows, but GRUB's HTTP client compares "Content-Length: " case-sensitively and then reads every file as empty. This transport writes canonical header names, keeps connections alive (GRUB sends HEAD then GET on one connection), and streams bodies.

archon-boot/pretty.ts

The boot server's window (spec 004, Article 19; spec 049): a rendering of structured events, never their source. Each event (telemetry/events.ts) is one line: an icon and tone chosen by its name (and, for boot files, which file), the time and address dimmed, the host's name highlighted, success green and problems red. Debug events (GRUB's harmless probing) are kept out unless verbose; the same event within a few seconds is shown once. boot.log and the OTLP log records hold every event.

archon-boot/stall.ts

Spec 051: a machine that takes the installer image and then goes quiet. Ubuntu's network installer holds the whole image in memory; with too little RAM (below about 8 GiB) it stalls before asking for its configuration, and nothing on the boot server's screen says so. This watch notices: after the image is served to an address, the installer asks for its configuration from that address within minutes, or the boot window explains.

archon-boot/telemetry.ts

The boot server's own telemetry (spec 023). Deno's built-in OpenTelemetry sends OTLP/JSON to a receiver inside the boot server (127.0.0.1:4319), which writes it to local files only: one OTLP JSON line per batch, the format OpenTelemetry's file exporter and otlpjsonfile receiver use, in daily files kept 30 days and 256 MB at most. Nothing leaves the PC; when otel-tui runs on the PC (OTLP on 127.0.0.1:4318), each batch is also handed to it.

archon-boot/tftp.ts

A read-only TFTP server for PXE (spec 004): UEFI PXE firmware fetches shim over TFTP, shim fetches GRUB, and GRUB its menu, kernel, and initrd, all from the same server. Each read is answered by the same handler as HTTP, so PXE and HTTP Boot serve identical files and menus. RFC 1350 with the blksize (2348), tsize (2349), timeout (2349), and windowsize (7440) options; block numbers roll over past 65535 (Ubuntu's initrd is ~100 MB).

archon/apply/apply.ts

archon apply: converge a host to its plan (Article XI). Idempotent: a run right after a successful run reports zero changes. Never removes anything (Article IX).

archon/apply/apt.ts

apt with real progress (spec 018): APT::Status-Fd=2 makes apt report "pmstatus:<pkg>:<percent>:<text>" and "dlstatus:..." lines on stderr, which drive the progress bar; everything else goes to the run log. apt's warnings are translated into problems with a fix instead of being pasted raw.

aptInstall(
p: Phase,
pkgs: string[]
): Promise<AptResult>

Install packages. When a maintainer script fails (often a transient problem during a large first install, such as an initramfs rebuild triggered mid-run), finish pending setup with dpkg --configure -a and try once more; only a second failure is reported as one.

f
aptUpdate(p: Phase): Promise<AptResult>

apt-get update: waits for another apt holding a lock, and retries network-shaped failures with backoff (spec 009). A failure that stays network-shaped is a warning; anything else is a failure.

f
classifyAptLine(line: string): AptIssue | undefined

Turn apt's W:/E: lines into one actionable issue per cause.

f
dpkgFailureParser(): { failures: DpkgFailure[]; feed(line: string): void; error(
pkg: string,
reason: string
): void; }

Collect "dpkg: error processing package X (--configure):" and the reason on the following line, so a failure names the package instead of apt's "Sub-process /usr/bin/dpkg returned an error code (1)".

I
AptIssue

One problem found in apt's output, worded for people, with a fix when there is one.

  • fix: string

    What to run or check to fix it.

    A warning (apt's W:) or a failure (E:, Err:).

  • message: string

    What went wrong.

  • network: boolean

    DNS, unreachable, or timed out: retried, then a warning (spec 009).

I
AptResult

How an apt run ended.

  • network: boolean

    It failed for network reasons only (warned, not failed).

  • ok: boolean

    Whether it succeeded (a network-only failure is not ok, but is only warned).

I

A package dpkg failed to install or configure.

  • cause: string

    The script's last output before dpkg gave up: usually the real cause.

  • pkg: string

    The package's name (without architecture).

  • reason: string

    dpkg's reason, from the line after its error.

archon/capabilities/etckeeper.ts

033-etckeeper: /etc's history in a local git repository (Ubuntu's etckeeper package): a commit before and after every apt run, one a day for anything else, and one per archon apply with its specs (spec 033). Archon sees drift only in files it manages; etckeeper records every change to /etc, and who made it. The history holds secrets (shadow, SSH host keys, the mail relay's password file), so it stays local and root-only, and is never given a remote (Article 13).

archon/capabilities/mail.ts

027-mail: every server can send mail, the way programs expect to (/usr/sbin/sendmail, or SMTP on localhost:25). Postfix, Ubuntu's default mail server, runs as a send-only "null client" (Postfix's STANDARD_CONFIGURATION_README): it receives nothing from the network, delivers nothing locally, and relays everything to Cloudflare Email Service over implicit TLS on port 465 with the fleet's API token (SASL). Cloudflare signs with DKIM for the sending domain. Mail for local accounts (root, ops, cron's MAILTO) goes to the fleet's mailbox; every sender becomes <user>+<host>.<tag>@<domain> (root+alpha.lab@example.net): one onboarded domain for the fleet, the machine in the subaddress (RFC 5233).

archon/capabilities/passwords.ts

037-smb, 039-pg-identity: one PAM hook keeps the copies of a person's Linux password that other protocols need in step with Linux: Samba's NT hash (SMB clients cannot prove a password any other way) and PostgreSQL's SCRAM verifier (for a published instance). Run by PAM, through Ubuntu's own pam-auth-update, after a password is accepted (auth: a login with a password, sudo, Cockpit) or changed (passwd). Real accounts only (UID 1000 and up; not root or ops); service accounts have no password.

Functions

f

Variables

v
PASSWORD_SYNC: `#!/bin/sh # Rendered by archon from specs 037-smb and 039-pg-identity. Do not edit. # Run by PAM (pam_exec expose_authtok) after a password was accepted (auth) or # changed (password): Samba and PostgreSQL get the same password for the same # account. Nothing is stored anywhere else. case "\${PAM_TYPE:-}" in auth|password) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac u="\${PAM_USER:-}" [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != ops ] && [ "$u" != root ] || exit 0 uid=$(id -u "$u" 2>/dev/null) || exit 0 [ "$uid" -ge 1000 ] || exit 0 pw=$(tr -d '\\000') [ -n "$pw" ] || exit 0 if [ -x /usr/bin/smbpasswd ]; then printf '%s\\n%s\\n' "$pw" "$pw" | /usr/bin/smbpasswd -s -a "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 fi # PostgreSQL, only while it is on (an opt-in service); in the background, so a login never waits. if [ -x /usr/local/bin/archon ] && /usr/bin/systemctl is-enabled --quiet postgresql.service 2>/dev/null; then # PAM gives the hook almost no environment: archon gets root's. ( printf '%s' "$pw" | HOME=/root PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \\ /usr/local/bin/archon pg passwd-sync "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 & ) fi exit 0 `

The PAM hook: keeps Samba's and PostgreSQL's copies of a person's password in step with Linux.

039-pg-identity: the fleet's service accounts on every server. An app runs as its own Linux account (s-<app>), the same UID everywhere, with no password and no shell; that account is its identity in PostgreSQL (peer on the socket).

archon/capabilities/web.ts

032-web: every server is HTTPS-ready from its first boot. Traefik (the official release binary, installed by the tools sync) on 80 and 443, open to everyone at the server's firewall, and no network allowlist behind it: who reaches the server is the router's decision (the firewall at the edge, outside the machine). The Archon Console (archon web serve, loopback only, spec 065) answers https://<host>.<domain> and any name or address nothing else claims. Podman (Ubuntu's package) is the container runtime: containers that carry traefik.enable=true get <container>.<host>.<domain>.

web(): Capability

HTTPS from the first boot: Traefik, the Archon Console, and Cloudflare DNS (spec 032).

archon/capabilities/workstation.ts

020-workstation: Ubuntu on WSL (or a desktop) as an Archon workstation. Only the user-level parts of a host apply: the tools at their newest releases, the dotfiles (fish, oh-my-posh, tmux, git), .mcp.json for the operator's own MCP client (spec 030), the archon command, and Ubuntu's daily updates. Nothing that belongs to a server: no installer, netplan, firewall, SSH hardening, ops account, converge timers, or backups. The checkout is /srv/archon, owned by the workstation's user.

archon/console/forms.ts

Specs 065 and 066: every command a console offers is a form, generated from the command registry (the source of archon help, the man pages, and the MCP tools), so the web and the CLI cannot drift. A form's values become an argument list for that command alone: each value is one argument (never a shell), checked against the command's own definition.

A form's values as cmd's argument list. Positional arguments first, in order, then the options; a flag is present when its box is ticked. Values may not start with "-" (they would read as options). Required ones must be there. Unknown fields are ignored.

archon/console/pam-worker.ts

Spec 065: the worker thread that runs pamCheck (PAM blocks for about two seconds after a wrong password; the web server keeps answering). Messages: {id, service, user, password} in; {id, ok} out.

archon/console/pam.ts

Spec 065: checks a username and password with Linux itself (PAM). The console calls it in a worker thread (pamAuthenticator): pam_unix waits about two seconds after a wrong password, and the web server must not stop answering meanwhile. The service is archon-console (/etc/pam.d/archon-console: common-auth and common-account, as Ubuntu's own services use them); the console's account is in the shadow group, so pam_unix can read the password hashes.

archon/core/announce.ts

Tell a running boot server something happened on this PC (spec 004): an event (spec 049) it records and shows in its window and boot.log. Arming, for example, is only a file the server reads when a machine contacts it, so without this the window stays silent until the host network-boots. Loopback only; best effort: no server running is not an error.

archon/core/lock.ts

One archon run at a time per host (specs 012, 017). The reconcile timer applies every 15 minutes; without this it could apply, or fetch, in the middle of someone's archon update or bootstrap. Children of a run that holds the lock (bootstrap and update hand-offs, reconcile's apply) inherit it through ARCHON_LOCK_HELD instead of waiting for their own parent.

archon/core/registry-types.ts

Types for the command registry (Article VI). One definition per capability generates the CLI, MCP tools, man pages, fish completions, and the agent's permission rules.

The tier this run needs (a command's tier can depend on its arguments, for example --check).

Parse argv for this command, or throw a message naming the problem (a person-only option from an agent is refused).

Interfaces

I
ArgSpec

One argument of a command: an option (--name) or a positional value.

  • default: string | boolean

    Its value when it is not given.

  • description: string

    What it does, in one line (help, man page, MCP).

  • human: boolean

    Only a person types it (--confirm-destroy, Article 23; --show for a secret): never offered over MCP, and refused when an agent runs the command (ARCHON_AGENT is set).

  • name: string

    Its name (the option is --name).

  • positional: boolean

    Given without --name, in order.

  • repeatable: boolean

    May be given more than once; the values are joined with newlines.

  • required: boolean

    The command refuses to run without it.

  • short: string

    A one-letter form (-m for --message).

  • type: "string" | "boolean"

    A value, or a flag.

I
Command

One archon command: its name, help, tier, arguments, and what it runs. The man pages, the MCP tools, and archon help all come from these.

  • aliases: string[]

    Other names for it (spec 060: stolos push is stolos apply).

  • args: ArgSpec[]

    Its arguments.

  • asOwner: boolean

    Always runs elevated, even when read-only, because it works through the checkout's owner (ops and the host's deploy key): push. Operators and the admin are in archon-ops, so sudo does not prompt (spec 006).

  • description: string

    Paragraphs separated by blank lines.

  • examples: Array<{ cmd: string; text: string; }>

    Examples, for its man page.

  • mutateWith: string

    The reverse: read-only, except with this flag, which changes the host (fs s3 key --rotate). It then elevates, and counts as mutate over MCP.

  • name: string

    Space-separated words, for example "tools sync".

  • noMcp: boolean

    Hide from MCP (for example mcp itself).

  • operation: boolean

    An operation (Article XXII): runs in phases with a header, a run log, and a closing summary instead of printing a result.

  • place: Place

    Where it runs: "pc" (stolos, in the fleet repository on your PC), "machine" (archon, on each server or workstation), or "both".

  • precheck: (
    args: Parsed,
    ctx: RunContext
    ) => Promise<number | undefined>

    A look before elevating (spec 038): when it returns a code, the command is already satisfied and finishes unprivileged, so an idempotent mutate command (archon pg ensure) works unattended for a normal user once its work is done.

  • readOnlyWith: string

    Tier when this flag is set (for example apply --check is read-only).

  • run: (
    args: Parsed,
    ctx: RunContext
    ) => Promise<number>

    Runs it; returns the exit code.

  • seeAlso: string[]

    Related man pages.

  • summary: string

    One line, for archon help.

  • tier: Tier

    What it may do: read, write the repository, change the host, or destroy (spec 030: MCP serves up to the fleet's tier).

  • unlocked: boolean

    Touches only its own files (archon notify's spool): no host lock, so it never waits for or blocks an apply, and it leaves the prompt's last-run segment alone.

I
RunContext

What every command is given besides its arguments.

  • hostName: string

    The host this invocation operates on.

  • json: boolean

    --json: machine-readable output, nothing drawn.

  • verbose: boolean

    -v: every item, as it happens.

archon/core/share.ts

The shared checkout (specs 001, 016): /srv/archon belongs to its owner (ops) and the archon-ops group, group-writable, so every operator can run archon and git there. Files a command writes (state/, out/, prov) must stay that way: as root they would otherwise be root-owned and read-only to the group, and a later archon capture as yourself fails with EACCES.

archon/doctor/doctor.ts

archon doctor (spec 026): a quick, read-only look at whether this machine can reach what it depends on, with what is wrong and where to look. It uses Ubuntu's own network tools (ip, ping, resolvectl, dig, chronyc, ufw, snap, mtr) and curl's timings; the endpoints come from this machine's own configuration (apt sources, the checkout's remote, the tools catalog, the fleet model), never from a list kept here. It changes nothing.

f
doctor(
host: HostDef,
o: { trace: boolean; send?: string; }
): Promise<number>

archon doctor: runs each read-only phase (link, Internet, endpoints, email) and prints what it finds. With trace, adds a path trace to unreachable endpoints; with send, mails the email findings. Returns 0: the closing summary counts the problems.

archon/doctor/email.ts

archon doctor's email checks (spec 026, for specs 025 and 027), shared by servers and the boot machine: the sending domain's records in DNS, the relay's credential, a login to the relay that sends nothing, and on servers Postfix itself. The records are the ones Cloudflare's Email Sending onboarding creates (developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/configuration/domains/). With send (archon doctor --send, and by itself after mail-setup, an install, or a new token), it also mails what it found to the shared mailbox through each path: archon's own sender, and on servers Postfix.

stolos workstation add (spec 020): run inside Ubuntu on WSL (or on an Ubuntu desktop), from the checkout in /srv/archon, as your own user. It writes fleets/<fleet>/hosts/<name>/host.ts (kind "workstation") and then, through sudo, converges the user-level parts: tools, dotfiles, the archon command, Ubuntu's daily updates (archon update --no-pull).

archon/mcp/server.ts

archon mcp: a Model Context Protocol server over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited), implemented natively without an SDK (Article II). Every registry command within the tier limit is a tool; docs, specs, runbooks, and reports are resources. Workstations reach it on a server as ops over SSH, forced to archon mcp --max-tier <tier> (spec 030): the limit is enforced here, on the server, whatever the client is configured to do.

archon/model/durable.ts

044-durable (Article 23): data that can come from end users is either durable (it exists nowhere else) or ephemeral (losing it is harmless). The operator chooses, for every source of such data, when turning it on; there is no default. A host is durable when anything on it is durable, and ephemeral otherwise; nothing about the class is stored, it is worked out from the host's records each time. A missing or unreadable choice counts as durable. Home directories on servers are ephemeral by rule: they are archived locally, and the login banner says they are not kept across a reinstall.

Evidence of data without a recorded choice counts as durable (Article 23).

The secret inventory (spec 028, constitution Article 13): every secret the fleet depends on, by name, where it lives, and how to make it again. Values never. The boot machine's secrets are what deno task stolos vault backs up and restores (spec 029); the owner's are listed so a lost one is not a surprise. A test checks that every path the code writes is listed here.

A file Archon keeps on a host: its content, owner, and mode, checked before and after it is put in place.

  • content: string

    Its content (absent for a symlink).

  • group: string

    Its group (default: the owner's).

  • mode: string

    Its mode, for example "0644".

  • onChange: Action[]

    What to do when it changed: reload, restart, run.

  • owner: string

    Its owner (a Unix account).

  • path: string

    Its absolute path on the host.

  • postValidate: string[]

    A command that checks it after it is in place (rolled back when it fails).

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that writes it.

  • symlink: string

    Make it a symlink to this target instead.

  • validate: string[]

    A command that checks the new content before it is put in place (the file's path appended).

I
FirewallPolicy

A firewall policy of the gateway, as UniFi lists it.

  • action: "allow" | "allow-return" | "block"

    Allow, allow return traffic only, or block.

  • exceptPorts: Port[]

    Every port except these.

  • from: { zone: Zone; network?: string; cidr?: Cidr; }

    Where traffic comes from: a zone, optionally one network or prefix of it.

  • id: number

    UniFi's policy number, as listed in the network reference.

  • ipVersion: "ipv4" | "both"

    IPv4 only, or both IPv4 and IPv6.

  • name: string

    Its name in UniFi.

  • ports: Port[]

    Ports matched, or matched by exception ("all ports except").

  • protocol: "tcp" | "udp" | "tcp/udp" | "any"

    The protocol it matches.

  • purpose: string

    Why it exists, in one line.

  • to: { zone: Zone; address?: IPv4; }

    Where it goes: a zone, optionally one address.

I
FleetDef

The fleet: one identity shared by every host (spec 003), in fleets/<id>/fleet.ts of a fleet repository. stolos fleet init <id> writes the first one from your GitHub account; edit it freely after, then stolos build.

  • admin: { user: string; uid: number; github: GitHubIdentity; }

    The fleet's admin: one person, one account on every host (spec 003).

  • id: string

    The fleet's id: its folder, fleets/<id>/, and a DNS label (lowercase, digits, hyphens).

  • keyboard: string

    The console's keyboard layout, for example "us".

  • locale: string

    For example "en_US.UTF-8".

  • mail: { to: string; domain: string; tag?: string; relay?: string; }

    Outbound mail (spec 027) and notifications (spec 025). Every server relays its mail (Postfix) through Cloudflare Email Service, from <user>+<host>.<tag>@<domain> (only <domain> onboarded for Email Sending in Cloudflare); mail for local accounts (root, ops) and archon's own messages go to to. Without it, no mail leaves and archon notify is not configured.

  • mcp: { maxTier?: McpTier; keys?: string[]; }

    The agent layer (spec 030, Article 17): workstations reach each server as ops over SSH, forced to archon mcp --max-tier <maxTier>. Default: tier mutate, the admin's GitHub SSH keys. The destructive tier is never served.

  • network: Partial<NetworkDef>

    The fallback network facts (spec 009) for a host that is not on a site network (a workstation). A host on the site takes them from its network.

  • observability: Partial<ObservabilityDef>

    Local observability limits for every host and workstation (spec 021).

  • providers: Partial<ProvidersDef>

    DNS, mail, and ACME providers (spec 046); see ProvidersDef for the defaults.

  • repository: { slug: string; url: string; branch?: string; }

    The GitHub repository hosts converge to; branch defaults to main (tests use their own).

  • services: ServiceDef[]

    Service accounts for apps, the same on every server (spec 039): Linux system accounts named s-<app>, with fixed UIDs, no password, no shell. An app runs as its account and reaches PostgreSQL as the role of that name.

  • signers: SignerDef[]

    Who may approve changes (spec 047): loaded from fleets/<id>/signers.ts.

  • site: SiteDef

    The site's network as data (spec 028, Article 21): fleets/<fleet>/site.ts.

  • ssh: { passwordFrom?: string[]; }

    SSH (spec 007): networks (CIDR) from which passwords are accepted as well as keys. Default: the private ranges (your LAN and VLANs). [] means keys only.

  • telemetry: { collector?: string; name?: string; }

    A central OpenTelemetry collector (spec 024). Hosts and workstations look for one every 15 minutes, by unicast DNS only (Article 20): this address, else the name (default "otel.localdomain", a UniFi Local DNS record) on port 4318. Until one answers, everything stays local.

  • timezone: string

    An IANA time zone, for example "America/New_York".

  • title: string

    Its name, for people.

  • ubuntu: { release: "26.04"; codename: "resolute"; point?: string; }

    The Ubuntu release every host runs (point: a point release's image, when pinned).

  • web: WebFleetDef

    HTTPS on every server (spec 032): each answers as <host>.<domain> and its apps as <app>.<host>.<domain>, with one Let's Encrypt certificate per server (the name and its wildcard) through Cloudflare's DNS challenge. Each server keeps its own A records in Cloudflare (private addresses). Without it, servers still answer HTTPS with a self-signed certificate.

I
GitHubIdentity

A GitHub account as gh reports it (spec 003). Public data only.

  • email: string

    GitHub's anonymized commit address: <id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com.

  • id: number

    GitHub's numeric account id (it never changes, unlike the login).

  • login: string

    The GitHub login.

  • name: string

    Profile name, or the login when the profile has none.

  • sshKeys: string[]

    Public SSH keys from https://github.com/<login>.keys.

I
GitHubSource

Where an upstream tool's releases come from (GitHub releases, each asset checked against GitHub's SHA-256).

  • asset: (
    arch: "amd64",
    version: string
    ) => RegExp

    The release asset's file name, for this architecture and version.

  • repo: string

    The GitHub repository, "owner/name".

  • tagPrefix: string

    What precedes the version in its tags (for example "v").

I
GuestDef

An LXD instance on a host (spec 017).

  • cpus: number

    CPU cores (default: LXD's).

  • data: DataClass

    Required (Article 23, spec 044): "durable" when the guest can hold data that exists nowhere else (backed up with lxc export and guarded), or "ephemeral" when losing it is harmless. There is no default.

  • image: string

    LXD image, for example "ubuntu:26.04".

  • kind: "container" | "vm"

    A system container, or a virtual machine.

  • memory: string

    For example "4GiB".

  • name: string

    The guest's name (an LXD instance name).

  • web: { port: number; https?: boolean; }

    Publish the guest's web port as <guest>.<host>.<domain> (spec 032).

I
HostDecisions

What operators decided for a host, in Git (spec 047): fleets/<id>/hosts/<host>/decisions.ts, written by stolos decide. A decision here wins over the host's own record.

  • optIns: Record<string, OptInRecord>

    What operators decided in Git (decisions.ts): opt-in name to its record.

I
HostDef

A host: one machine of the fleet, in fleets/<id>/hosts/<name>/host.ts. stolos host add <name> --claim (or --mac-address) writes a server's; stolos workstation add a workstation's. What it gets comes from its capabilities; what it is (its MAC, its SSH host keys) is in its registration.ts, from the machine itself (spec 051).

  • arch: "amd64"

    The CPU architecture (amd64 only, for now).

  • backup: Partial<BackupDef>

    Overrides of the default backup policy (spec 016).

  • capabilities: Capability[]

    What it gets: foundation() for a server, workstation() for a workstation, plus any more.

  • desktop: boolean

    Workstations (spec 036): a graphical desktop, not WSL or a headless machine. VS Code is installed only here; set by stolos workstation add.

  • disk: DiskDef

    Servers: the install disk (default: Ubuntu's LVM layout on the largest disk).

  • dnsName: string

    Its unicast DNS name, a UniFi Local DNS record (Article 20): "alpha.localdomain".

  • guests: GuestDef[]

    LXD containers and VMs (spec 017).

  • ip: string

    Its fixed address (a UniFi Fixed IP), inside its network (spec 028).

  • ipv6: boolean

    Per-host override of the network's IPv6 (spec 009).

  • kind: "server" | "workstation"

    "server" (default): an Ubuntu Server host Archon installs and converges. "workstation" (spec 020): Ubuntu on WSL (or a desktop) where Archon applies only the user-level parts: tools, dotfiles, the archon command.

  • mac: string

    Optional, and no longer written by archon: the NIC the host network-boots from (lowercase, colon-separated). Since spec 051 the MAC lives in registration.ts, given with --mac-address or reported by the machine; a mac here is still read. Without either, the host is recognized by a claim or its own Boot URI (/boot/<name>/bootx64.efi).

  • name: string

    Its name: a DNS label, unique in the fleet.

  • network: string

    The site network it lives on (spec 028), by name: "Servers". Its IPv6 follows that network.

  • observability: Partial<ObservabilityDef>

    Overrides of the fleet's local observability limits (spec 021).

  • optIn: Record<string, OptInRecord>

    Opt-in services and containers an operator turned on or off (spec 040): this machine's archon.sql<name>.json {enabled, by, at}. Read by loadHosts; never written in a host file. Absent means off.

  • outOfBand: { amt?: { address?: string; notes?: string; }; }

    Out-of-band management (Intel AMT): its address and notes, for the person at the console.

  • pg: { instances?: PgInstanceDef[]; }

    PostgreSQL instances this server keeps (spec 038).

  • pgState: PgState

    What operators recorded on this host (the host's own archon.sql (opt-in pg), spec 038): the clusters Archon created and which are published. Read by loadHosts; never written in a host file.

  • registration: HostRegistration

    Who it is, from fleets/<id>/hosts/<host>/registration.ts (spec 047): read by loadHosts.

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that brought it (for a host, usually "004-install").

  • switchPort: string

    The switch port it is cabled to: "flex-2.5g/3".

  • user: string

    Workstations: the existing account Archon sets up (default: the fleet admin's name).

  • users: UserDef[]

    Extra accounts beyond the fleet admin and ops.

  • web: { routes?: Array<Omit<WebRoute, "spec">>; }

    Services this server publishes through its proxy (spec 032).

I
HostPlan

Everything a host gets: every capability's contribution, merged, for apply and verify.

  • aptRepos: AptRepoDef[]

    Every vendor apt repository.

  • checks: CheckDef[]

    Every check.

  • files: FileDef[]

    Every file.

  • fleet: FleetDef

    Its fleet.

  • host: HostDef

    The host.

  • notes: Record<string, string[]>

    Notes, by spec.

  • packages: PackageDef[]

    Every package, from every capability.

  • ports: PortDef[]

    Every open port.

  • routes: WebRoute[]

    Every service published through the proxy.

  • specsUsed: SpecId[]

    The specs its capabilities come from.

  • tools: ToolDef[]

    Every tool.

  • units: UnitDef[]

    Every unit.

  • users: UserDef[]

    Every account on it.

I
HostRegistration

Who a host is, in Git (spec 047): fleets/<id>/hosts/<host>/registration.ts, written by stolos host add. Public facts only: its SSH host public keys (operators' known_hosts is generated from them), its network card, and the fingerprint of its read-only deploy key.

  • added: string

    When it was registered (ISO date).

  • deployKey: string

    SHA256:... of its deploy key, when it has one.

  • mac: string

    The network card it is recognized by when it network-boots (spec 051).

  • macSource: "operator" | "installed"

    Where that MAC came from (spec 051): "operator", given with --mac-address; "installed", reported by the machine itself when it installed (or was bootstrapped). Only a machine that installed as this host is reinstalled without the blank-disk guard.

  • sshHostKeys: string[]

    "ssh-ed25519 AAAA...", "ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 AAAA...", "ssh-rsa AAAA..." (no comments).

I
LocalDnsRecord

A UniFi Local DNS record: a name that resolves to an address on the site.

  • address: IPv4

    The address it resolves to.

  • name: string

    The name, for example "alpha.localdomain".

I
NetworkDef

The network a host lives on (spec 009).

  • ipv6: boolean

    Does this network route IPv6? false (an IPv4-only LAN): apt resolves and connects over IPv4 only, and retries transient failures.

I
ObservabilityDef

Local observability (spec 021). Every store is ephemeral: each has an age and a size limit, and gives way first when the disk runs low. The limits are upper bounds, not promises.

  • logsMaxSize: string

    ...in at most this much space (journald also keeps 15% of the disk free).

  • logsRetention: string

    journald: kept up to this long (journald syntax, for example "3month")...

  • metricsDays: number

    PCP metric archives: kept up to this many days...

  • metricsMaxSize: string

    ...and pruned, oldest first, beyond this size (for example "2G").

  • minFreePercent: number

    Below this much free disk (percent), metric archives are pruned regardless of age.

  • tracesDays: number

    Archon's own traces, metrics, and logs (OTLP files): kept up to this many days, 64 MB at most.

I
OptInRecord

An operator's decision about an opt-in service or container (spec 040).

  • at: string

    When (ISO time).

  • by: string

    Who decided (a Unix account).

  • data: DataClass

    For an opt-in that holds end users' data: the operator's choice (spec 044).

  • enabled: boolean

    On or off.

I
PackageDef

A package to install, from Ubuntu's apt (default), a PPA, a vendor repository, or a snap.

  • debconf: string[]

    Answers to the package's own install questions, as debconf-set-selections lines ("postfix postfix/main_mailer_type select No configuration"), set before it is installed: Ubuntu's way to install a package unattended.

  • name: string

    The package's name.

  • ppa: string

    The upstream maintainers' Launchpad PPA ("owner/name") that carries newer builds (Article 5). Added with add-apt-repository, kept current by unattended-upgrades; without builds for this release, Ubuntu's package stays.

  • repo: string

    A vendor's own apt repository (AptRepoDef.id) that carries this package.

  • source: "apt" | "snap"

    apt (default) or snap: both are native on Ubuntu (Article 2).

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that installs it.

I
Persona

A persona's definition: what it means and what it brings (spec 012).

  • definition: string

    What it means, in one sentence.

  • features: { fish: boolean; tmux: boolean; devTools: boolean; }

    What it turns on.

  • groups: string[]

    Linux groups it adds.

  • id: PersonaId

    Its id.

  • implies: PersonaId[]

    Personas it includes (an operator is also a developer).

  • label: string

    Its name, for people.

I
PgDatabaseDef

A database in an instance and who may use it (spec 039). Every name is a Linux account (a person in the model, or a service account s-<app>) or

  • extensions: string[]

    Extensions Archon creates (as the superuser, for untrusted ones).

  • name: string

    The database's name.

  • owner: string

    Owns the database and its public schema (creates tables).

  • read: string[]

    Read every table.

  • write: string[]

    Read and write every table (not create).

I
PgInstanceDef

A named PostgreSQL instance: one Debian cluster, <version>/<name> (spec 038).

  • databases: PgDatabaseDef[]

    The databases in it, and who may use each.

  • environment: string

    Shown in the psql prompt: production, staging, development... (default production).

  • name: string

    The instance's name (a Debian cluster name): "prime" is the default one.

  • port: number

    Fixed port (default: the first free from 5432, then kept).

  • protected: boolean

    psql turns AUTOCOMMIT off and warns in red (default true for production).

  • version: number

    Major version (default 18, Ubuntu's).

I
PgRecord

One instance as recorded on the host (the host's own archon.sql (opt-in pg)).

  • by: string

    Who created it.

  • created: string

    ISO time and who: Archon owns only clusters it created (FR-003).

  • environment: string

    Shown in the psql prompt.

  • port: number

    The port it listens on.

  • protected: boolean

    psql turns AUTOCOMMIT off and warns in red.

  • published: { at: string; by: string; }

    Published: reachable on the server's address over TLS (scram-sha-256). From anywhere the router lets through (the machine restricts no network).

  • retired: number[]

    Older clusters kept, stopped, after an upgrade (removed with archon pg remove --version).

  • version: number

    Its major version.

I
PgState

the host's own archon.sql (opt-in pg): the opt-in switch (spec 040) and the instances Archon made.

  • instances: Record<string, PgRecord>

    Each instance Archon created, by name.

I
PortDef

A port opened in the host's firewall (ufw).

  • port: number

    The port number.

  • protocol: "tcp" | "udp"

    tcp or udp.

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that opens it.

I
ProvidersDef

The fleet's outside providers (spec 046), each a closed set the engine implements. Defaults: Cloudflare for DNS and mail, Let's Encrypt for ACME.

  • acme: "letsencrypt" | "letsencrypt-staging"

    Certificates (spec 032). "letsencrypt-staging" gives untrusted certificates with generous rate limits: for synthetic and test fleets.

  • dns: "cloudflare"

    DNS: each server's records and the ACME DNS challenge (spec 032).

  • mail: "cloudflare"

    Outbound mail: the SMTP relay (Cloudflare Email Service, spec 027).

I
ServiceDef

An app's own Linux account (spec 039).

  • description: string

    Its purpose, in one line.

  • name: string

    s-<app>: lowercase letters, digits, and dashes.

  • uid: number

    Fixed, so the account is the same on every server: 800 to 899.

I
SignerDef

Who may approve changes to a fleet (spec 047, Article 9): a host applies only a tip of main signed by one of these keys. Kept in fleets/<id>/signers.ts, written by stolos signers.

  • added: string

    When it was added (ISO date).

  • key: string

    The public key: "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..." (or sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com).

  • name: string

    A short name, the principal in allowed_signers ("alice-daily").

  • role: "daily" | "recovery"

    daily: approves changes; recovery: kept offline, replaces a lost or stolen daily key.

I
SiteDef

The site's network as data (spec 028, Article 21): fleets/<fleet>/site.ts. Archon checks hosts against it and renders the network reference from it; it never changes the router.

  • bootServer: { host: string; address: IPv4; network: string; tftp: Port; http: Port; }

    The boot machine: where network installs come from (TFTP and HTTP ports).

  • ddns: { provider: "cloudflare"; record: string; type: "A"; proxied: boolean; zone: string; }

    Names only: the token stays in UniFi.

  • devices: Device[]

    Devices with known addresses.

  • dns: { upstream: IPv4[]; autoDns: boolean; localRecords: LocalDnsRecord[]; }

    DNS: the gateway's upstream resolvers, and the Local DNS records.

  • gateway: { model: string; name: string; network: string; }

    The gateway: its model, its name, and the network it lives on.

  • mdnsProxy: { networks: string[]; services: string[]; }

    The gateway's mDNS proxy (reflector): which networks, which services.

  • name: string

    The site's name.

  • networks: SiteNetwork[]

    Every network.

  • policies: FirewallPolicy[]

    Every firewall policy, in UniFi's order.

  • security: { ips: string; upnp: boolean; portForwards: number; inbound: string; }

    Security settings: IPS, UPnP, port forwards, and inbound traffic, as configured.

  • wifi: WifiNetwork[]

    Every Wi-Fi network.

  • wireguard: { name: string; listen: Port; endpoint: string; network: string; clients: Array<{ name: string; address: IPv4; }>; reach: Zone[]; }

    Names and endpoints only: keys stay in UniFi and on the clients.

  • zones: Zone[]

    The firewall zones in use.

I
SiteNetwork

A network of the site: its VLAN, prefix, gateway, firewall zone, DHCP, and what it routes.

  • cidr: Cidr

    Its IPv4 prefix.

  • cidr6: string

    A VPN's IPv6 prefix (ULA), when it has one.

  • dhcp:
    { from: IPv4; to: IPv4; leaseSeconds?: number; }
    | "unifi-managed"
    | "static-per-client"

    Who hands out addresses: a DHCP range, UniFi's own management, or a fixed address per client.

  • gateway: IPv4

    The gateway's address on it.

  • ipv6: boolean

    Does this network route IPv6 to hosts? (spec 009: apt and Postfix use IPv4 only when not.)

  • mdnsReflect: boolean

    In the gateway's mDNS proxy (reflector) scope. Never for Servers or DMZ (Article 20).

  • name: string

    Its name, as UniFi shows it (for example "Servers").

  • netboot: { server: IPv4; file: string; }

    UniFi's Network Boot (DHCP next-server and file).

  • notes: string

    Anything a person should know about it.

  • vlan: VlanId

    Its VLAN; absent for a VPN, which has no VLAN.

  • zone: Zone

    Its firewall zone.

I
ToolDef

A tool installed at its newest release (spec 010): from apt, a snap, an upstream binary (checked, smoke-tested, rolled back on failure), or its own installer.

  • bins: string[]

    The commands it provides, linked into /usr/local/bin.

  • forPersona: PersonaId

    Only for users with this persona.

  • github: GitHubSource

    Where upstream releases come from (upstream-binary tools).

  • id: string

    Its id (also its folder under /opt/tools).

  • installer: string

    The URL of its own installer script (self-updating tools).

  • name: string

    Its name, for people.

  • package: string

    The apt package, when it is not the id.

  • ppa: string

    apt tools: the maintainers' PPA with newer builds (PackageDef.ppa).

  • repo: AptRepoDef

    apt tools: the vendor's own apt repository (PackageDef.repo).

  • restarts: string[]

    Services restarted after this tool is installed or upgraded (for example its own daemon).

  • serverOnly: true

    Installed on servers only (the HTTPS front door, spec 032).

  • source: "apt" | "snap" | "upstream-binary" | "self-updating"

    Where it comes from: Ubuntu's apt, a snap, an upstream release binary, or its own installer (which then updates itself).

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that brings it.

  • unprivileged: true

    The tool refuses to run as root (Steampipe): its smoke test and its verify check run as nobody when archon runs as root.

  • verify: string

    The command that checks it works (its smoke test after an install, and a verify check).

  • versionCommand: string

    The command that prints its version.

  • workstationOnly: true

    Installed on workstations only (the agent layer, spec 030), never on servers.

I
UnitDef

A systemd unit Archon manages: its file (when Archon writes it), and whether it is enabled, started, or masked.

  • content: string

    The unit file's content, when Archon writes it.

  • generated: boolean

    Made by a systemd generator (a Podman Quadlet container, spec 040): it cannot be enabled; its [Install] section starts it at boot unless masked. Turning it on is unmask and start.

  • managed: boolean

    Archon writes the unit file (true) or only enables, starts, or masks Ubuntu's own (false).

  • onCalendar: string

    For a timer: when it fires (systemd OnCalendar syntax).

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that brings it.

  • start: boolean

    Start it now, not only at the next boot.

  • state: "enabled" | "disabled" | "masked" | "ignore"

    masked: stopped and masked, the package kept (spec 001: avahi-daemon).

  • switch: string

    An operator's switch (spec 037): the name of a record in this machine's archon.sql<switch>.json. When it says {"enabled": true} the unit is enabled and started; otherwise state applies (masked, for SMB).

  • unitName: string

    The systemd unit's name, for example "archon-web.service".

  • verify: string

    The command that checks it (exit 0: fine).

I
UserDef

A person's account on a host (spec 012): the fleet admin, or one of a host's extra users.

  • admin: boolean

    In the sudo group.

  • email: string

    Their address, for git and notifications.

  • fullName: string

    The person's name (GECOS).

  • name: string

    The Unix account name.

  • personas: PersonaId[]

    What they do here: their groups and tools follow.

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that brought them.

  • sshKeys: string[]

    The public SSH keys that may log in as them.

  • uid: number

    A fixed UID, the same on every host (default: assigned by Ubuntu).

I
WebFleetDef

HTTPS for every server (spec 032): names under one domain, certificates from Let's Encrypt.

  • acmeEmail: string

    Let's Encrypt account address (default: fleet.mail.to).

  • domain: string

    The DNS zone suffix servers live under, for example "lab.example.net".

  • zone: string

    The Cloudflare zone that holds it (default: the last two labels, "example.net").

I
WebRoute

A service published through the server's proxy (spec 032) as <name>.<host>.<domain> (who reaches it is the router's decision).

  • address: string

    The backend's address (default 127.0.0.1).

  • description: string

    What it is, in one line (shown on the server's welcome page).

  • https: boolean

    The backend speaks HTTPS (certificate not checked; loopback or guests only).

  • name: string

    A DNS label: the app's subdomain.

  • port: number

    The backend's port.

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that publishes it.

I
WifiNetwork

A Wi-Fi network (SSID) and the network it puts clients on.

  • bands: Array<"2.4" | "5" | "6">

    The bands it broadcasts on (GHz).

  • guest: boolean

  • network: string

  • notes: string

    Its security.

    Its SSID.

archon/notify/notify.ts

archon notify (spec 025): major events, by email, to the fleet's shared mailbox. Reporting never fails or slows the action it reports: a message is queued on disk and sent by archon notify flush (a service started at once and a timer every 5 minutes) through Cloudflare's SMTP relay (spec 027), with backoff when it cannot be reached, duplicates dropped by key within an hour, and one summary after a long outage. Nothing secret is ever sent (redact.ts).

archon/notify/watch.ts

archon notify watch (spec 025, user story 2): the events an operator must hear about even when nothing in Archon ran. It follows the journal (Ubuntu already records every one of them: sshd, sudo, su, login, useradd, the kernel, systemd) and turns the few that matter into messages; nothing is added to sshd, PAM, or auditd (Article 2). Every ten minutes it also looks at what the journal cannot say: disk space and the authorized_keys files.

archon notify watch (the watch service): check keys, boot and disk, then follow the journal and send a message for each signal that matters. Every ten minutes it checks keys and disk again and summarizes failed logins (at most one summary an hour); it exits 0 to restart on a new checkout. Returns 1 if journalctl ends, so systemd restarts it.

archon/observe/discover.ts

archon observe discover (spec 024): find a central OpenTelemetry collector and forward this machine's telemetry to it. By unicast DNS only (Article 20: never mDNS or DNS-SD): the fleet model's address, else the name "otel.localdomain" (fleet.telemetry.name, a UniFi Local DNS record). A candidate counts only if it accepts OTLP. What is found goes into a second Collector config file, merged with the base one: journald, PCP (through pmproxy), and Archon's own OTLP are then forwarded, with a bounded queue on disk. Until a collector answers, the file is empty and everything stays local.

archon/optin/optin.ts

040-opt-in: opt-in services and containers. Every server has them; each is off until an operator turns it on, and then on (across applies, reboots, and reinstalls) until an operator turns it off. The decision is the host's own record, this machine's archon.sql<name>.json {enabled, by, at}: model input for every plan (loadHosts), and the switch of the opt-in's unit at apply time (UnitDef.switch). Where an opt-in can use Linux accounts and their credentials, it does; where its protocol needs a secret of its own, the identity is still the Linux account and only that account can read it. Every opt-in that can hold end users' data (spec 044, Article 23) is turned on with a forced choice, --durable or --ephemeral, kept in the same record.

MAINTAIN_SQL: { connections: `SELECT coalesce(datname, '-') || ' ' || coalesce(state, 'background') || ' ' || count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY datname, state ORDER BY 1`; max: `SHOW max_connections`; sizes: `SELECT datname || ' ' || pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) FROM pg_database WHERE NOT datistemplate ORDER BY pg_database_size(datname) DESC`; bloat: `SELECT schemaname || '.' || relname || ' ' || n_dead_tup || ' dead of ' || (n_live_tup + n_dead_tup) || ' (' || round(100.0 * n_dead_tup / greatest(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 1)) || '%)' FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE n_dead_tup > 1000 ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC LIMIT 10`; }

The queries archon pg maintain reports: connections, max_connections, database sizes, and dead rows.

  • bloat: `SELECT schemaname || '.' || relname || ' ' || n_dead_tup || ' dead of ' || (n_live_tup + n_dead_tup) || ' (' || round(100.0 * n_dead_tup / greatest(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 1)) || '%)' FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE n_dead_tup > 1000 ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC LIMIT 10`
  • connections: `SELECT coalesce(datname, '-') || ' ' || coalesce(state, 'background') || ' ' || count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY datname, state ORDER BY 1`
  • max: `SHOW max_connections`
  • sizes: `SELECT datname || ' ' || pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) FROM pg_database WHERE NOT datistemplate ORDER BY pg_database_size(datname) DESC`

archon/pg/tui.ts

archon pg admin-tui (rainfrog) and archon pg observe-tui (pgcenter top): each finds the instance the way archon pg show does (an instance Archon keeps, any cluster here, or a service section) and starts the tool already connected. On this server: the socket and you as yourself (peer, no password). With --remote: the published name over TLS, verify-full against the system's roots. A password never goes on a command line (other users see those in ps): rainfrog asks for it; pgcenter gets it from ~/.pgpass or, asked here, in its own environment only.

The agent layer's project configuration (spec 030, Articles 4, 6, 17), rendered from the model for a workstation's checkout: .mcp.json with one MCP server per server host (archon-<fleet>-<host>, reached as ops over SSH; spec 046: one repository can hold several fleets, and two may name a host alike). archon/s3/s3.ts

041-s3: S3 object storage (RustFS), an opt-in container (spec 040), managed with archon fs s3. Identities are Linux accounts: every person on the server and every fleet service account has an S3 user of the same name, allowed the buckets named <name>-*. S3 signs requests with a secret the server keeps, so it cannot use the Linux password (Archon never puts a Linux password where it can be read back): each account's secret is generated on the server, and only that account (and root) can read it.

archon/telemetry/events.ts

Spec 049-telemetry (Article 27): events are structured at their source. Each event has a declared name (below), a severity, the host and address it is about, attributes, and a message; it is recorded as an OpenTelemetry log record. Anything a person reads (the boot server's window, boot.log) is a rendering of these records, never the source: the window's icons, colors, and de-duplication come from the event's name and attributes, not from parsing its text.

archon/telemetry/signals.ts

Spec 049-telemetry (Article 27): every signal Archon emits, declared once. The telemetry module accepts only these names (TypeScript checks every call), man 7 archon-telemetry is rendered from this list, and the tests read it.

Interfaces

I
MetricSpec

What a metric measures.

  • attributes: string[]

    Attributes beyond the run's own (archon.command, archon.fleet, host).

  • description: string

    What it counts or measures.

  • group: Group

    Its group.

  • kind: "counter" | "histogram" | "gauge"

    Its kind.

  • unit: string

    Its unit.

Type Aliases

T
Group = "health" | "security" | "state"

Spec 049-telemetry (Article 27): every signal Archon emits, declared once. The telemetry module accepts only these names (TypeScript checks every call), man 7 archon-telemetry is rendered from this list, and the tests read it.

T
MetricName = keyof METRICS

A metric's name (from METRICS).

archon/tools/catalog.ts

Tool catalog (spec 010, Article 5): the newest stable release of each tool, from its maintainers' PPA or the vendor's own apt repository when there is one (apt keeps it current), else its official binary release (checksum-verified), else Ubuntu's archive (tmux). Nothing is built from source.

Functions

f
installPathFor(t: ToolDef): string | undefined

Where an upstream binary tool installs (/opt/tools/<id>); undefined for apt-installed tools.

Variables

v
TOOLS: ToolDef[]

Every tool Archon installs, with where it comes from and how it is verified.

archon/vault/restore.ts

Spec 061: deno task stolos vault restore <zip> makes a freshly cloned PC the boot machine again from one backup ZIP (spec 056). It reads the ZIP and checks every file against its manifest, puts each file back where stolos keeps it (the secrets, readable by you only; the daily key in .ssh; the recovery key in the key store), records the ZIP as the last backup, then runs keys setup (Git's signing for this checkout, and one test signature: your daily passphrase) and gets VS Code its types.

archon/vault/zip.ts

Spec 056: the boot machine's backup is one ZIP file. deno task stolos vault backup writes it into the backup folder where archon keeps its data (Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\stolos\backup; Linux: ~/.local/share/stolos/backup), reads it back to check every file, and tells you to put it wherever you keep important things safe. It holds everything this PC would need again after a disaster: every fleet's secrets (the admin password's hash, each server's SSH host keys and deploy key, the Cloudflare tokens, carried certificates) and your signing key (both halves; the private half stays locked by its passphrase). On a freshly cloned PC, vault restore <zip> (spec 061) puts it all back; RESTORE.txt in every ZIP says the same, with the steps by hand.

archon/web/acme.ts

032-web: a server's Let's Encrypt certificates survive its re-install. Before deno task stolos boot reinstall reboots a server, it copies Traefik's ACME store (the Let's Encrypt account, the certificates, and their keys) to the boot machine; the install hands it back, and the first boot puts it in place before Traefik first starts. Traefik then serves the trusted certificate from its first minute and asks Let's Encrypt only to renew (Let's Encrypt allows 5 identical certificates a week). Renewals stay on the server: the boot machine only carries the store across the re-install, and an expired copy is never delivered.

archon/web/config.ts

032-web: the server's HTTPS front door, as data. Traefik (an official release binary, spec 010) listens on 80 and 443; 80 only redirects. No route is limited by network: who reaches the server is the router's decision (the firewall at the edge, outside the machine; Article 21 and spec 064). Certificates come from Let's Encrypt through Cloudflare's DNS challenge when fleet.web is set; until then (and without it) Traefik's self-signed certificate answers.

archon/web/markdown.ts

035-welcome-guide: the repository's guides (docs/*.md) as HTML on the welcome page, so one text serves the repository, the man pages, and the server. Handles what those guides use: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code blocks, blockquotes, inline code, bold, italics, and links. Everything is escaped first; links to other guides stay on the page, the rest go to GitHub.

archon/web/serve.ts

archon web serve (specs 032, 035): the welcome page and the guides on 127.0.0.1:8090, behind Traefik. archon/web/welcome.ts

032-web and 035-welcome-guide: the welcome page every server shows at https://<host>.<domain> (and at any name or address nothing else claims), written for someone new to the server: what it is, whether it's healthy, its apps, what's installed and how to use it, and how changes are made. Rendered per request by archon web serve (loopback only, behind Traefik, local networks only). No secrets: the mailbox address and the admin's username are the most personal things on it. Plain text only (no Nerd Font glyphs).

  • url: string

    Its HTTPS address (for example https://cockpit.alpha.lab.example.net).

I
WelcomeData

Everything the welcome page shows, gathered per request by archon web serve.

  • address: string

    The server's address on the local network, if known.

  • admin: string

    The fleet admin's username (for the ssh command shown).

  • agent: AgentSetup

    How an AI agent reaches this server (spec 035); servers only.

  • backup: { last?: string; ok?: boolean; }

    The last backup run, when the host has the backup timer: when it ended and whether it succeeded.

  • certificate: { issuer: string; notAfter: string; }

    The certificate Traefik serves on 443: its issuer and expiry, as openssl prints them.

  • data: { class: "durable" | "ephemeral"; reasons: string[]; }

    Article 23 (spec 044): durable or ephemeral, and why.

  • fqdn: string

    Its full name (for example alpha.lab.example.net); unset without fleet.web.

  • generated: string

    When the data was gathered: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC.

  • guide: GuideItem[]

    What is installed and how to use it, from the host's plan (spec 035).

  • guides: Array<{ name: string; title: string; }>

    Guides served at /guide/<name>.

  • host: string

    The host's name in the model.

  • installed: { at?: string; ok?: boolean; checks?: { passed: number; total: number; }; }

    The install record (spec 048): when, whether it succeeded, and its checks.

  • lastRun: { command: string; failures: number; warnings: number; deferred: number; push: boolean; at: string; }

    Archon's last run on this host (its status file): the command, its counts, whether commits wait to be pushed, and when.

  • mailbox: string

    The fleet's mailbox, where alerts go; unset without mail.

  • os: string

    "Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS"

  • repo: { slug: string; url: string; }

    The fleet repository: owner/name and its GitHub URL.

  • services: Service[]

    The apps and pages behind the proxy (none without fleet.web).

  • title: string

    The fleet's title.

  • unrouted: number[]

    Ports open to the network with nothing published (internal ones excluded).

  • updates: { pending?: number; reboot: boolean; rebootPackages: string[]; lastRun?: string; }

    Ubuntu's updates: how many wait (unset when unknown), whether a reboot is needed and for which packages, and when they last installed by themselves.

  • verify: { at: string; passed: number; total: number; failed: string[]; }

    The last archon verify: when, how many checks passed of how many, and which failed.

mod.ts

Stolos: the fleet engine

Interfaces

I
FleetDef

The fleet: one identity shared by every host (spec 003), in fleets/<id>/fleet.ts of a fleet repository. stolos fleet init <id> writes the first one from your GitHub account; edit it freely after, then stolos build.

  • admin: { user: string; uid: number; github: GitHubIdentity; }

    The fleet's admin: one person, one account on every host (spec 003).

  • id: string

    The fleet's id: its folder, fleets/<id>/, and a DNS label (lowercase, digits, hyphens).

  • keyboard: string

    The console's keyboard layout, for example "us".

  • locale: string

    For example "en_US.UTF-8".

  • mail: { to: string; domain: string; tag?: string; relay?: string; }

    Outbound mail (spec 027) and notifications (spec 025). Every server relays its mail (Postfix) through Cloudflare Email Service, from <user>+<host>.<tag>@<domain> (only <domain> onboarded for Email Sending in Cloudflare); mail for local accounts (root, ops) and archon's own messages go to to. Without it, no mail leaves and archon notify is not configured.

  • mcp: { maxTier?: McpTier; keys?: string[]; }

    The agent layer (spec 030, Article 17): workstations reach each server as ops over SSH, forced to archon mcp --max-tier <maxTier>. Default: tier mutate, the admin's GitHub SSH keys. The destructive tier is never served.

  • network: Partial<NetworkDef>

    The fallback network facts (spec 009) for a host that is not on a site network (a workstation). A host on the site takes them from its network.

  • observability: Partial<ObservabilityDef>

    Local observability limits for every host and workstation (spec 021).

  • providers: Partial<ProvidersDef>

    DNS, mail, and ACME providers (spec 046); see ProvidersDef for the defaults.

  • repository: { slug: string; url: string; branch?: string; }

    The GitHub repository hosts converge to; branch defaults to main (tests use their own).

  • services: ServiceDef[]

    Service accounts for apps, the same on every server (spec 039): Linux system accounts named s-<app>, with fixed UIDs, no password, no shell. An app runs as its account and reaches PostgreSQL as the role of that name.

  • signers: SignerDef[]

    Who may approve changes (spec 047): loaded from fleets/<id>/signers.ts.

  • site: SiteDef

    The site's network as data (spec 028, Article 21): fleets/<fleet>/site.ts.

  • ssh: { passwordFrom?: string[]; }

    SSH (spec 007): networks (CIDR) from which passwords are accepted as well as keys. Default: the private ranges (your LAN and VLANs). [] means keys only.

  • telemetry: { collector?: string; name?: string; }

    A central OpenTelemetry collector (spec 024). Hosts and workstations look for one every 15 minutes, by unicast DNS only (Article 20): this address, else the name (default "otel.localdomain", a UniFi Local DNS record) on port 4318. Until one answers, everything stays local.

  • timezone: string

    An IANA time zone, for example "America/New_York".

  • title: string

    Its name, for people.

  • ubuntu: { release: "26.04"; codename: "resolute"; point?: string; }

    The Ubuntu release every host runs (point: a point release's image, when pinned).

  • web: WebFleetDef

    HTTPS on every server (spec 032): each answers as <host>.<domain> and its apps as <app>.<host>.<domain>, with one Let's Encrypt certificate per server (the name and its wildcard) through Cloudflare's DNS challenge. Each server keeps its own A records in Cloudflare (private addresses). Without it, servers still answer HTTPS with a self-signed certificate.

I
HostDef

A host: one machine of the fleet, in fleets/<id>/hosts/<name>/host.ts. stolos host add <name> --claim (or --mac-address) writes a server's; stolos workstation add a workstation's. What it gets comes from its capabilities; what it is (its MAC, its SSH host keys) is in its registration.ts, from the machine itself (spec 051).

  • arch: "amd64"

    The CPU architecture (amd64 only, for now).

  • backup: Partial<BackupDef>

    Overrides of the default backup policy (spec 016).

  • capabilities: Capability[]

    What it gets: foundation() for a server, workstation() for a workstation, plus any more.

  • desktop: boolean

    Workstations (spec 036): a graphical desktop, not WSL or a headless machine. VS Code is installed only here; set by stolos workstation add.

  • disk: DiskDef

    Servers: the install disk (default: Ubuntu's LVM layout on the largest disk).

  • dnsName: string

    Its unicast DNS name, a UniFi Local DNS record (Article 20): "alpha.localdomain".

  • guests: GuestDef[]

    LXD containers and VMs (spec 017).

  • ip: string

    Its fixed address (a UniFi Fixed IP), inside its network (spec 028).

  • ipv6: boolean

    Per-host override of the network's IPv6 (spec 009).

  • kind: "server" | "workstation"

    "server" (default): an Ubuntu Server host Archon installs and converges. "workstation" (spec 020): Ubuntu on WSL (or a desktop) where Archon applies only the user-level parts: tools, dotfiles, the archon command.

  • mac: string

    Optional, and no longer written by archon: the NIC the host network-boots from (lowercase, colon-separated). Since spec 051 the MAC lives in registration.ts, given with --mac-address or reported by the machine; a mac here is still read. Without either, the host is recognized by a claim or its own Boot URI (/boot/<name>/bootx64.efi).

  • name: string

    Its name: a DNS label, unique in the fleet.

  • network: string

    The site network it lives on (spec 028), by name: "Servers". Its IPv6 follows that network.

  • observability: Partial<ObservabilityDef>

    Overrides of the fleet's local observability limits (spec 021).

  • optIn: Record<string, OptInRecord>

    Opt-in services and containers an operator turned on or off (spec 040): this machine's archon.sql<name>.json {enabled, by, at}. Read by loadHosts; never written in a host file. Absent means off.

  • outOfBand: { amt?: { address?: string; notes?: string; }; }

    Out-of-band management (Intel AMT): its address and notes, for the person at the console.

  • pg: { instances?: PgInstanceDef[]; }

    PostgreSQL instances this server keeps (spec 038).

  • pgState: PgState

    What operators recorded on this host (the host's own archon.sql (opt-in pg), spec 038): the clusters Archon created and which are published. Read by loadHosts; never written in a host file.

  • registration: HostRegistration

    Who it is, from fleets/<id>/hosts/<host>/registration.ts (spec 047): read by loadHosts.

  • spec: SpecId

    The spec that brought it (for a host, usually "004-install").

  • switchPort: string

    The switch port it is cabled to: "flex-2.5g/3".

  • user: string

    Workstations: the existing account Archon sets up (default: the fleet admin's name).

  • users: UserDef[]

    Extra accounts beyond the fleet admin and ops.

  • web: { routes?: Array<Omit<WebRoute, "spec">>; }

    Services this server publishes through its proxy (spec 032).

Variables

v
VERSION: "0.70.0"

The engine's version (spec 046-engine-instance). A fleet imports the engine from GitHub (@stolos/ → raw.githubusercontent.com/.../v<VERSION>/src/), so every push to main raises it and the release workflow tags that commit v<VERSION>. deno task version bump raises the minor number (0.1.0, 0.2.0, ...); deno task version check fails when main already has this version.

stolos/main.ts

stolos (spec 059): the fleet's command, on your PC, in the fleet repository (deno task stolos ...). Everything about the fleet as a whole: creating it, keys and signers, adding and installing machines (stolos boot ..., the boot server), backups, and keeping this checkout up to date. Each machine has its own command, archon, for itself.
